scientific_queries.note: Bagged capacity control to settle whether pathway annotation adds anything beyond drug identity.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round finishes the control it started, and the answer overturns the programme's central negative.

design.why_bagging: a single random block is itself noisy, so the capacity control is averaged over ten independent blocks

what_this_means.the_central_negative_is_refuted: C45/C46/C49 concluded the annotation model was worthless; that comparison pitted coarse against fine granularity, and with a common encoding plus a capacity-matched control the annotation block adds +5.37 pp while random features add nothing
what_this_means.identity_and_annotation_are_complementar: pathway alone about 7.50%, identity alone 8.13%, together 12.75%, so the two sources carry complementary rather than redundant information
what_this_means.capacity_is_not_the_driver: the random control has exactly 171 dimensions like the combined model and scores 7.38%, below identity alone at 8.13%

scope_of_the_claim: one pool (unseen combinations), one dataset, one criterion. It does not show pathway annotation is strong alone, only that it is not redundant with drug identity.

consequence_for_promotion.status: identity+pathway at 12.75% is now the strongest predictor the programme has measured on this pool, so the earlier 'nothing is worth promoting' must be revisited
consequence_for_promotion.but: promotion still requires replication on the other two pools and on a second criterion, plus leakage and equal-budget controls

limits: one pool, one dataset, one criterion
does not establish that pathway annotation alone is strong
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: move identity+pathway to the joint-holdout and both-drugs-unseen pools, and to a second criterion, before any promotion

register_updates.C72: new and decisive: the annotation model is not useless
register_updates.SYNTHESIS: correction banner added at the top
